title: How to Add AI Voice Agents to VICIdial Without Replacing Your Infrastructure
summary: Learn how to add AI voice agents to VICIdial without replacing your dialer, SIP trunks, or campaigns. See the 3 integration methods and how SigmaMind deploys in minutes.
body_markdown:
If your outbound campaigns already run on VICIdial, you can evaluate voice AI without replacing the dialer. You may be able to retain your carrier and lead lists, but the pilot still requires campaign and routing changes. Check how VICIdial and the AI service will record and report outcomes separately.


You can use[Voice AI for VICIdial](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/vicidial-ai-integration-strategies) for first-touch conversations and lead qualification while VICIdial continues dialing. Whether a call can reach a person depends on the transfer destination and handoff you configure.


SigmaMind AI documents a VICIdial integration that keeps VICIdial responsible for dialing through your existing carrier. This article helps you decide where AI fits; the[VICIdial integration guide](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/vicidial-integration-guide.md) covers configuration and testing.


## **Why Do Call Centers Want to Add AI to VICIdial Without Replacing It?**


VICIdial is an open-source dialer that many outbound teams already use for their campaigns. Replacing VICIdial can require campaign reconfiguration, retraining, and changes to custom dialplans. Keeping it lets you test voice AI without taking on a full dialer migration.


You can test[call center voice AI](https://www.sigmamind.ai/) on suitable first-touch conversations and route calls that need a person to a configured destination. Measure qualification quality, transfers, and cost against your own campaign baseline before expanding. Keep consent checks and do-not-call (DNC) screening in your outbound process, and review applicable rules for AI-generated calls with counsel.


The practical question is whether you can add AI to a selected workflow while keeping VICIdial responsible for dialing. SigmaMind AI's documented approach uses a VICIdial Remote Agent bridge; it retains the existing outbound carrier number but requires routing and campaign configuration.


## **How Can You Add AI While Keeping VICIdial?**


In the documented integration, VICIdial dials through the existing outbound carrier. When a customer answers, VICIdial routes the call through a Remote Agent to SigmaMind AI's SIP server and bridges the call legs. This lets you retain VICIdial as the dialer, but it is not a configuration-free addition. See the[VICIdial integration guide](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/vicidial-integration-guide.md) for requirements and setup steps.


### What changes in a pilot


Plan for a VICIdial user and Remote Agent, carrier and routing entries, and campaign and lead-list configuration. The[VICIdial integration guide](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/vicidial-integration-guide.md) describes using the existing outbound carrier number. Validate routing and agent mapping before using a live campaign.


- **Keep:** VICIdial dialing through the existing outbound carrier number, as described in the integration guide
- **Configure:** The Remote Agent bridge, routing, agent mapping, and pilot campaign
- **Validate:** Call routing, recording access, any configured transfer destination, and failure handling before expanding


## **What Must a VICIdial Pilot Confirm?**


Check whether answered calls reach SigmaMind AI through the Remote Agent bridge and whether staff can review the resulting outcomes. A pilot should confirm each of the following:


1. VICIdial dials through the existing outbound carrier; the pilot still requires VICIdial routing and campaign configuration
2. Answered calls route through the configured VICIdial Remote Agent bridge to SigmaMind AI; if you use VICIdial campaign AMD (Answering Machine Detection), configure and test it for that campaign
3. SigmaMind AI follows the pilot's configured conversation and qualification criteria. Review a sample of calls to see whether it collects the information your campaign requires.
4. Test whether calls can reach the intended human destination and what information the agent receives. Do not assume a warm transfer, whisper, or conversation summary is available without confirming the required configuration or custom integration.
5. Agree on how staff will review and record qualification outcomes; do not assume SigmaMind AI automatically writes VICIdial disposition codes
6. Check VICIdial's call view separately from SigmaMind AI's[Conversations view](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/documentation/observe/monitor-calls.md) , and confirm which AI call details are available for review.


Confirm whether supervisors need both the VICIdial Real-Time Screen and SigmaMind AI's Conversations view. Decide how they will reconcile call records for quality review and reporting.


## **Which VICIdial Settings Need Review?**


You can retain VICIdial as your dialer and keep the existing outbound carrier number, but the integration does require configuration. Before piloting a[voice AI agent with VICIdial](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/vicidial-agent-assist-architectures-use-cases-guide) , review these settings and records:


- **Existing campaigns:** Choose a pilot campaign and review its Remote Agent routing and settings. Do not assume its configuration remains unchanged.
- **SIP trunks and carriers:** VICIdial can continue dialing through the existing outbound carrier number, but the AI bridge requires carrier and routing configuration.
- **Lead lists and CRM data:** Check the pilot lead-list settings and establish which data, if any, the AI needs. Verify how that data will be passed before relying on it.
- **Disposition codes:** Decide how staff will enter VICIdial dispositions and reconcile them with AI call outcomes before relying on a combined report.
- **Call recordings:** Check where each system stores recordings and which recordings your configuration produces. Apply recording and retention requirements to each location.
- **Supervisors and monitoring:** Check the VICIdial Real-Time Screen and SigmaMind AI's Conversations view separately to determine what staff can monitor and review.


## **What Call Types Should You Start With When Adding AI to VICIdial?**


Start with one campaign whose outcomes you can check against a baseline. Use it to test routing, conversation quality, and any required handoff. The following call types call for different checks:


- **Lead qualification campaigns:** Define the questions and qualification criteria, then test any configured transfer to a person.
- **Payment reminder outreach:** Review applicable consent, collections, disclosure, and recording requirements with your compliance team or counsel before testing how outcomes are recorded.
- **Appointment confirmation and scheduling:** Test confirmations first. Verify calendar access and update permissions before offering booking or rescheduling.
- **Re-engagement campaigns:** Check whether contacts can lawfully be called, then test how the AI identifies interest and routes calls that need a person.
- **After-hours inbound routing:** Treat this as a separate inbound-routing use case. Verify that your phone-system configuration can send those calls to the AI before including it in a pilot.


For the documented Remote Agent setup and its testing requirements, see the[VICIdial integration guide](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/vicidial-integration-guide.md) .


## **VICIdial AI Pilot Questions**


Use these questions to establish what your proposed connection supports before approving a pilot:


**Does adding AI require downtime on my VICIdial server?**


Do not assume a downtime-free setup. The Remote Agent integration requires VICIdial routing and campaign configuration; plan and test changes under your normal change-control process.


**What happens if the AI goes offline mid-campaign?**


The documentation does not establish automatic overflow if the AI connection fails. Decide how the pilot campaign should handle an unavailable Remote Agent, then test that behavior before production use.


**Will the AI work with my current VICIdial version?**


The published integration guide does not provide a tested version matrix. Check your VICIdial version and configuration against the guide with the SigmaMind AI team before committing to a pilot.


**Can I run AI on one campaign while keeping others human-only?**


A selected campaign is a sensible pilot scope. Configure its Remote Agent routing and verify that campaigns intended to stay human-only are unaffected before broadening the rollout.


**Does TCPA compliance change when I add AI to VICIdial?**


You remain responsible for assessing which rules apply to your campaign, including consent, do-not-call screening, AI-call disclosures, calling limits, pacing, and recording notices. Review the campaign with counsel where appropriate. Do not assume the VICIdial–SigmaMind AI integration enforces these controls.


## **Is Adding AI to VICIdial the Right Next Step for Your Call Center?**


If your VICIdial team spends substantial time on repetitive first-touch conversations, a limited AI pilot may be worth testing. Keep VICIdial as the dialer, but budget for Remote Agent routing and campaign configuration. Set success criteria for conversation quality, human handoffs, reporting, and cost before expanding.


Expand only after you have checked routing, any configured human handoff, the records available in each system, and measured campaign outcomes. Confirm any reporting or analytics connection separately rather than assuming the systems provide a combined view.
